capabilities.target: payments-agent pay_vendor task carrying vendor, bank details, and amount

instructions.note: The only safeguard against paying a fraudulent vendor is the prompt instruction 'Only pay vendors on the approved list,' which checks vendor identity but not bank account details, and is enforced solely by model compliance.

'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks' assumes downstream verification that the runtime notes show does not exist: payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task with no further check.

The agent is told to 'choose the best' quote and use its bank details with no instruction to verify those details against a trusted vendor record, leaving quote selection and payment-detail sourcing entirely to model judgment over untrusted content.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: This human decision does not weaken with model capability, but it is made before any vendor quote or bank detail exists and its record is not passed to payments-agent, so it provides no protection for the eventual payment capability regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Approved-vendor-list prompt instruction
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced only through the system prompt instruction 'Only pay vendors on the approved list.' It is applied by the model, checks vendor identity only and not bank account details, and a more capable model can be reasoned or injected past it, especially when untrusted content spoofs an approved vendor's identity.

controls.name: SSO authentication of the purchase requester
Bank-detail verification against vendor system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. If added, payment would require bank details to match a verified vendor-onboarding record rather than the quote itself, making attacker-supplied bank details in a quote irrelevant to where money is sent.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval immediately before payment
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. A gate showing the approver the actual vendor, bank account, and amount immediately before payment, reviewed individually, would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Signed and pinned payments-agent card
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Pinning or hashing the agent card and verifying it on each use would prevent silent redefinition or impersonation of payments-agent regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Tamper-evident payment audit log
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. A log entry written outside the model's control, binding approval reference, vendor, bank details, amount, and triggering input, would make payment actions attributable regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Bind manager approval scope to the delegated payment task
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Carrying a verifiable approval reference (vendor, bank details, amount) into the task sent to payments-agent, and requiring payments-agent to check it, would prevent the orchestrator's general delegation authority from being used beyond what was actually approved.

findings.title: TC1-style: untrusted vendor quote supplies the bank details used for an irreversible delegated payment

attack_path.note: Untrusted vendor email supplies the quote and its bank details
Agent checks the vendor name against the approved list; bank details are not checked
Agent delegates payment to payments-agent using the bank details from the untrusted quote

forecast.watch_signal: subject.model version changes, or the median number of steps/tool calls per purchase cycle rises; also watch for payments whose bank details differ from a vendor's previously used account.

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to choose the best vendor quote and use the bank details from that quote, with the only stated safeguard being that the vendor must be on the approved list.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task, with no check that those details match a verified vendor record.

recommendations.action: Verify bank account details against a vendor-onboarding system of record, not the quote itself, before payment; block payment on mismatch.
Require a raw-action human approval step, reviewed individually, showing vendor name, bank details, and amount together immediately before payment.
Log and alert when a payment's bank details differ from the vendor's previously used details.

findings.title: TC7: budget approval is laundered into unverified authority for payments-agent to pay a specific vendor and bank account

attack_path.note: Employee requests a purchase (item and budget only)
Manager approves item and budget before any quote or vendor is known
Orchestrator delegates payment; the approval record is not passed, so payments-agent cannot verify this specific payment was approved

threat_refs.name: Autonomous AI Agent Communication: Direct Agent Communication

forecast.watch_signal: Additional payment-capable peer agents added to the orchestrator's delegation targets without bound approval context, or removal of the vendor-list check.

evidence.observation: The manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists.
The approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.

recommendations.action: Bind a verifiable approval reference, including vendor and bank details once known, into the task sent to payments-agent, and require payments-agent to check it before paying.
Require a second, specific approval once vendor and bank details are known, rather than treating the initial budget approval as sufficient authority for the final payment.

findings.title: Insecure A2A channel to payments-agent: unpinned agent card and static shared bearer token enable peer impersonation or redirection

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

forecast.watch_signal: New A2A peer agents are added, or the bearer token used against payments-agent is shared more widely, without a card-pinning or mutual-auth policy.

evidence.observation: The card declares only a bearer authentication scheme, with no signature or pinning metadata.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token.

recommendations.action: Pin or hash the payments-agent agent card and verify it before each use; block delegation on mismatch.
Replace the static shared bearer token with mutual TLS or a signed, short-lived identity assertion between orchestrator and payments-agent.

findings.title: No attributable audit record ties a specific approval to a specific delegated payment

forecast.watch_signal: Confirm at deployment whether a tamper-evident payment log exists; its absence at go-live is the signal to re-run this assessment.

evidence.locator: prompt.md and runtime notes (full artifact set)
evidence.observation: No logging, audit trail, or provenance mechanism is described anywhere in the design for payment delegation.

recommendations.action: Record a tamper-evident log entry for every delegated payment including the approval reference, vendor, bank details, amount, and triggering input, written outside the model's own output.

stride_coverage.rationale: The orchestrator's own outbound communications beyond the payment delegation are not described in the artifacts, so disclosure risk here cannot be assessed.
Each approved purchase request results in at most one payment delegation per the described flow; no looping or resource-exhaustion construct is described for the orchestrator itself.
Artifacts do not describe what payments-agent logs, returns, or exposes about payment details to other systems or consumers.
payments-agent processes one delegated payment task at a time in this design; no amplification or flood vector is described.
Artifacts do not describe any mechanism, such as signed email or verified sender identity, for proving which party actually sent a given vendor quote.
Artifacts do not describe how the manager's approval action itself is authenticated, for example whether it goes through the same SSO system as the purchase request.
Artifacts do not describe who can edit the approved vendor list or what controls, such as change review, govern updates to it.
The vendor list is read internally by the orchestrator only; no capability in this design sends its contents outside the organization.
The vendor list is a static reference read on each request; it is not a target for flooding or resource exhaustion in this design.
This flow carries vendor-supplied content into the orchestrator; it does not carry internal confidential data outward, so outbound disclosure does not apply to this flow.
Artifacts do not describe any rate limiting or volume control on inbound vendor emails processed by the orchestrator.
Artifacts do not confirm what protections, beyond TLS implied by the HTTPS endpoint, apply to bank details and amounts carried on this flow, for example field-level encryption or log redaction.
Each approved purchase request produces at most one payment delegation call in this design; no loop or amplification mechanism is described.

rating.rationale: The orchestrator uses bank details drawn directly from untrusted, externally supplied vendor quotes to trigger an irreversible, broadly credentialed payment delegation (ASI01/ASI02/ASI03), guarded only by a behavioral 'approved vendor' name check that does not verify bank details; inherent is critical and residual is high. Separately, the manager approval meant to authorize the purchase is granted before any vendor or bank detail is known and its record never reaches payments-agent, laundering budget approval into unverified payment authority (TC7; high inherent, moderate residual, since the behavioral vendor check is the only thing on this path). The A2A channel to payments-agent uses an unsigned, unpinned agent card and a static shared bearer token, so peer identity cannot be verified (ASI04; high/high, no mitigating control exists). No audit trail or action provenance is described for payment delegation, leaving actions unattributable if something goes wrong (ASI10 repudiation; high/high). The single highest-leverage fix is a structural check that verifies payment bank details against a vendor-onboarding record independent of the quote, combined with a raw-action, low-volume human approval immediately before payment. The control whose decay moves the forecast most is ctl.vendor_list_check: it is the only control credited on the primary path, it is behavioral and dependent, and removing it under a model upgrade or longer task horizon returns the main finding to its critical inherent level.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or source code was provided; capability scope for payments-agent's own validation logic is inferred from the runtime notes alone, so confidence on some findings is medium rather than high.

Enforcement of the approved budget ceiling against the final payment amount was not described one way or another; if a hard spend cap tied to the approved budget exists, it was not evidenced and could not be credited as a control.
